articles.title: Grammy Latino 2026: Urias, de Uberlândia, conquista um gramofone | G1
articles.standfirst: Em seu discurso, a artista, premiada na categoria Melhor Álbum de Rock ou Música Alternativa em Língua Portuguesa, fez um agradecimento especial à Liniker.
articles.summary: A cantora Urias, de Uberlândia, conquistou o Grammy 2026  na categoria Melhor Álbum de Rock ou Música Alternativa em Língua Portuguesa por 'Carranca'.
articles.body:
Urias recebe o Grammy Latino em Las Vegas — Foto: Reprodução/YouTube

A cantora Urias, de Uberlândia , conquistou o Grammy 2026 na categoria Melhor Álbum de Rock ou Música Alternativa em Língua Portuguesa por 'Carranca'. A uberlandense concorria com Black Pantera, de Uberaba, e ainda Detonautas, Foto em Grupo e Chico Chico, filho de Cássia Eller (1962-2001).

Urias é cantora, compositora, dançarina e modelo. Nascida e criada em Uberlândia, ganhou projeção nacional em 2019, com o lançamento de 'Diaba', sua primeira música autoral.

"Eu nem tô acreditando no que tá acontecendo, quando eu escrevi esse agradecimento não tinha caído a ficha ainda. Por ser quem eu sou, fui treinada e ensinada de que coisas boas não seriam possíveis de acontecer comigo", disse a artista no início do discurso.

Urias agradeceu aos seus Orixás, produtores, compositores aos empresários, às participações especiais do álbum, à equipe e a todos que acreditaram nela e ouviram o álbum.

A artista fez um agradecimento especial à Liniker, a quem chamou de irmã, e quem segundo ela, 'escancarou as portas para a próxima passar'.

"Hoje eu acredito que eu alcei voo. Obrigada!", disse ela, emocionada.

Urias tem três álbuns gravados: 'Fúria' (2022), 'Her Mind' (2023) e o agora premiado com o Grammy Latino 'Carranca' (2025), todos lançados pela Mataderos.

A artista uberlandense mistura elementos do pop, R&B e música eletrônica. Além da música, Urias também trabalha como modelo e já participou de edições do São Paulo Fashion Week. Mulher trans, a cantora também é uma das vozes em defesa dos direitos da população LGBT+.

Depois de se mudar para São Paulo, há cerca de 7 anos, ela retornou à cidade na turnê de 'Her Mind', em 2023. Já em 2024, Urias recebeu o Título de Honra ao Mérito em homenagem ao Mês da Mulher na Câmara de Uberlândia.

articles.title: Dolly Parton’s Final Vocals Featured on ‘Torn,’ a Duet with Bono from U2 Recorded Just Weeks Before Her Death
articles.summary: ‘Torn’ appears on U2’s new album ‘Carnaval De Luz’ set for release on Nov. 13, with a country version of ‘Torn’ featuring Parton premiering on Thursday, Nov....
articles.body:
Dolly Parton's vocals feature on U2's new song "Torn," taken from their new album, Carnaval De Luz, which is set for release on Friday, Nov. 13

The duet between the late country music star and Bono was recorded in June 2026, just weeks before her death at 80 in August

A country version of the track is receiving an all-day radio premiere on Nov. 12 before U2's album arrives Friday

Months after her death, Dolly Parton 's final vocals are here!

On Thursday, Nov. 12, a country version of "Torn," a duet between the late country music icon and Bono , premiered on Country Radio ahead of Carnaval De Luz , U2 's 16th studio album featuring the track, which goes on sale this Friday, Nov. 13.

"Torn" was co-written by U2, Parton and Johnny McDaid, according to a press release shared with PEOPLE. It is produced by Jacknife Lee and also features Daniel Lanois playing pedal steel.

The tender country song details broken family ties that hold wider resonances. The "Jolene" singer recorded the song in Nashville this past June, which makes it her final recorded vocal performance prior to her death at 80 years old on Aug. 25, 2026.

Parton's team promoted the upcoming song on social media , posting a sweet message shared with Bono, 66, for their collaboration.

"Hey Bono, Hope you like what I did. I did quite a few things. Take from it what you want and what you need, but I love the song, and I think it could be something really special," the post, dated June 2, read.

"Thanks for including me in your life. I've always loved you and always will," Parton added.

Ahead of "Torn"'s release on Friday, a country version titled "Torn" (Kent Wells Version) is set to receive an exclusive Country Radio World Premiere, airing all day on Thursday on all major radio broadcast media companies, including iHeart, Cumulus, Audacy, Beasley, Summit, Townsquare, and SiriusXM The Highway, Prime Country, and Y2Country, as well as the Music Choice platform.

"I can't deny this passion and desire / But I know it has to burn me / Standing this close to the fire / What am I supposed to do? / And how am I supposed to choose? / I love 'em both and I just feel so torn / I love 'em both and I just feel so torn," a snippet of the song's lyrics read.

"Torn apart these loving hearts / That beat and break the same / We share a house divided / And the blood that fills our veins / Brothers turn to strangers / And sons deny their name / Somebody loses either way / And every heart is torn," the stars later sing.

Bono told Rolling Stone that he struggles to listen to the tune following Parton's death. "When she got ill, she got out of her bed to sing this song. And you can hear that. And I can't even listen to it now," he told the outlet.

The posthumous track comes after Parton was featured on " Bound to Ride ," a tribute song for The Stanley Brothers , which was released around two weeks after her death.

Parton died after a "brief battle with cancer," reps for the "I Will Always Love You" singer confirmed to PEOPLE on Aug. 25.

"Our beloved Dolly Parton spent her life and career bringing joy, laughter, hope and integrity into everything she touched. Her unmatched generosity reached the lives of countless people whom she would never meet, yet she was always there to offer a helping hand," the statement read.

articles.title: Alanis Morissette calls out “Dogma” costar Ben Affleck for asking why she didn’t ‘lead with my sexuality’
articles.summary: Morissette then played a video of Affleck’s head exploding on a screen behind her during her “Butterfly With a Machete” show in Los Angeles.
articles.body:
Alanis Morissette called out Ben Affleck on stage during a Butterfly With a Machete show in Los Angeles.

The singer previously starred with Affleck in 1999's Dogma , and said the actor asked why she didn't "lead with my sexuality" at the time.

Morissette also targeted other celebs on stage, including Joni Mitchell, Sinead O'Connor, Tori Amos, Courtney Love, and Billy Corgan.

In addition to India, terror, and disillusionment, Alanis Morissette has thanked Dogma costar Ben Affleck for making what she said was a shady remark about her sexuality.

While on stage during Wednesday night's performance of her Butterfly With a Machete residency in Los Angeles (watch in Entertainment Weekly 's video below), Morissette relayed past struggles and obstacles she's faced throughout her career — including "harsh judgments" from media, the public, and even fellow stars during the height of her fame in the 1990s.

"I've even had a guy ask me why I didn't lead with my sexuality," Morissette told the crowd before quipping, "Thank you, Ben Affleck."

The crowd laughed as a scene from their 1999 film Dogma then played on a screen behind the singer-songwriter, depicting Affleck's head exploding.

EW has reached out to Affleck's representative for a response to Morissette's remarks on stage.

Earlier, Morissette elaborated on the criticism she endured after rising to global stardom upon the release of her masterwork album Jagged Little Pill in 1995.

Morissette told concertgoers that she faced "harsh judgments about my songs, about my body, about how I look, about how I think, about how I feel, about my value system, about my weight, about how feral I am, about how feral I live, about my approach to parenting, about my approach to education, my approach to freaking anything" at the time. She also added that she's faced scrutiny "about who I love" in her personal time.

Elsewhere during the concert, she told a story about trying to connect with actor Johnny Depp: "I did call Johnny Depp at one point, and his response was, 'Why are you calling me?'" she said, adding that she "was looking for a friend" amid her struggles.

She said at the concert that she also experienced issues with "the women I looked up to," and named Joni Mitchell, Sinead O'Connor, Tori Amos, and Courtney Love (as well as Billy Corgan) as people who "were ripping me apart publicly" throughout the decade.

"The sisterhood I so badly needed was truly nonexistent in the '90s. There were no girl squads then," Morissette said. "The women were competitive and vicious. The scarcity message was that there was one throne, and we were all fighting for it, and whoever was in it, kill her."

EW has reached out to Mitchell, Depp, Amos, Love, and Corgan for comment.

She did, however, note that there were "outspoken brothers" who supported her, including Elliot Smith and Tupac: "Those two were always very kind to me," she said.

Morissette previously opened up about her struggles in the entertainment industry in a 2021 documentary, Jagged , which she later criticized for having a "salacious agenda" and "reductive" story.

"Me not telling specific information about my experience as a teenager was almost solely around wanting to protect my parents, protect my brothers, protect future partners, protect myself, protect my physical safety," she said in the documentary of alleged sexual assault. "It was a lot of shame around having any kind of victimization of any kind, and it took me years in therapy to even admit that there had been any kind of victimization at my part. I'd always say, 'I was consenting,' then I'd be reminded, hey, you were 15. You're not consenting at 15. Now, I'm like, oh, yeah, they're all pedophiles. All statutory rape."

articles.title: Kylie Jenner sued by another former employee, fourth lawsuit in 7 months
articles.summary: Kylie Jenner has been sued again by a former housekeeper alleging workplace violations, discrimination, retaliation and wrongful termination.
articles.body:
Kylie Jenner has been sued by another former housekeeper alleging multiple workplace violations, disability discrimination, retaliation and wrongful termination.

Dinora Carolina Cabria Amaya filed the lawsuit against Jenner, 29, her company and staff members Laura Dooley and Itzel Sibrian in Los Angeles County Superior Court Thursday, Nov. 5, according to documents obtained by USA TODAY.

Amaya alleged that during her time as a housekeeper for Jenner's various properties from March 2025 until February, she did not receive proper pay, endured injuries due to the job – for which she was discriminated against – and then got fired for raising her concerns.

See photos of Kylie Jenner in her $50M Victoria's Secret Fashion Show bra

Jenner's attorney, Michael Rhodes, told USA TODAY in a Thursday, Nov. 12 statement: "These latest cases are being brought by the same lawyer who previously filed claims on behalf of Kylie's former household staff. It's clear that this lawyer wants to use publicity to try and extract an unwarranted payday. We're not going to be intimidated into doing that. As such, we'll defend these meritless cases vigorously and look forward to telling our side of the story."

This is the fourth lawsuit Jenner is facing from former employees, all of whom are represented by Della Shaker of Shaker Law Group .

Shaker addressed Amaya's new filing in a statement to USA TODAY: "To every housekeeper, nanny, caregiver, driver, chef, and domestic worker who has been afraid to speak up: your work matters, your dignity matters, and your rights matter."

She continued, "You do not lose your legal protections because you work inside a private residence or for a wealthy family. If you have experienced unpaid wages, discrimination, retaliation, or mistreatment, we encourage you to seek confidential legal advice. You deserve to be heard."

What does the latest lawsuit against Kylie Jenner allege?

In her filing, Amaya said she began her position in March 2025 on a six-day-per-week schedule of eight-hour shifts, reporting to managers Dooley and Sibrian. Almost immediately, she alleged she was "working more than eight hours per day due to Defendants demands" while still being "paid the same $40.00 hourly rate without overtime or double time" until May 2025.

She allegedly disclosed her complaints during a meeting with someone from human resources but alleged that "nothing was done to remedy the situation—however, [Amaya] was then added to payroll—provided with some overtime and meal break violation pay."

Kylie Jenner sued by former chef who alleges work led to miscarriage

In September, Amaya alleged that an "unsecured canister of pepper spray" was discharged into her face, which caused "ongoing physical impairments affecting her ability to perform certain job duties." However, the complaint alleges that the more she "complained that she was hurt, the harder Defendants made her job," including removing the other housekeeper who was helping her, requiring her to work alone, and assigning her heavier and more physically demanding tasks.

On another unspecified occasion, Amaya alleged she got locked inside Jenner's closet and was "confined against her will" for more than an hour. When she told Dooley she "was trapped and having a panic attack," Dooley allegedly "laughed and mocked her stating, 'No one is at the house that can let you out and I cannot give the password to anyone else, you just have to wait.'"

On Oct. 28, 2025, Amaya was assigned to clean a doghouse, where one of Jenner's dogs allegedly bit her. When she reported the injury to Dooley, "no meaningful assistance was provided," the filing alleged.

"By this point, Defendants knew [Amaya] had suffered multiple workplace injuries, sought medical treatment, continued experiencing physical symptoms, and repeatedly asked for help and reported numerous violations," according to the filing. "Instead of helping her, Defendants removed assistance, increased her workload, assigned heavier tasks, and abruptly changed her schedule and work locations. Defendants were making her life miserable so she would quit."

Celebrities taken to court, from Diddy to Weinstein and Russell Brand

Many stars have found themselves in courtrooms due to criminal charges — among them Sean "Diddy" Combs, Bill Cosby, Danny Masterson and Russell Brand. Others, like Gwyneth Paltrow and Johnny Depp, have publicly fought various civil lawsuits in court. Here's what happened in each case. If you or someone you know has experienced sexual violence, RAINN’s National Sexual Assault Hotline offers free, confidential, 24/7 support in English and Spanish via chat and at 800-656-4673 .

Additional incidents include failure to pay for mileage, vehicle expenses or travel time, despite Amaya allegedly learning from another housekeeper that they were being compensated. Amaya said she requested mileage in late January, and on Feb. 6, less than two weeks later, she was fired.

"As a direct and proximate result of Defendants' conduct, [Amaya] suffered lost earnings, lost employment benefits, emotional distress, humiliation, anxiety, and other damages according to proof," the lawsuit said.

Kylie Jenner legal trouble history, timeline

This case is the latest of many against Jenner this year. In April, former housekeeper Angelica Hernandez Vasquez filed a complaint alleging "a hostile work environment" in which she claims to have experienced "discrimination, harassment, and retaliation … based on her race, national origin, religion, and disability."

That same month, Juana Delgado Soto , also a previous housekeeper for "The Kardashians" star, sued for wrongful termination, discrimination, harassment, retaliation, failure to pay wages and intentional infliction of emotional distress.

In June, a private chef who once worked for Jenner went to court with more than two dozen claims , including discrimination, harassment, emotional distress, wrongful termination, retaliation and failure to pay proper wages.

articles.title: Michael Jackson did not create the iconic Thriller dance, claims choreographer Vincent Paterson, says Michael Peters was ‘wiped from history’ in biopic, leaving him deeply upset
articles.summary: Michael Jackson is synonymous with the iconic dance moves in his 1983 hit Thriller, but choreographer Vincent Paterson has claimed that the King of Pop
articles.body: Michael Jackson is synonymous with the iconic dance moves in his 1983 hit Thriller, but choreographer Vincent Paterson has claimed that the King of Pop did not create the famous choreography himself. In an interview with The Sun, Paterson, 76, alleged that the upcoming Michael Jackson biopic misrepresented the creative process behind the legendary music video by omitting choreographer Michael Peters, who actually developed the dance concept based on Jackson's vision. Deeply upset by the omission, Paterson says he wants to ensure Peters receives the recognition he deserves.Paterson, who worked closely with Jackson for nearly two decades, collaborated with choreographer Michael Peters and filmmaker John Landis on the making of Thriller. According to him, Peters was responsible for creating the choreography, while Jackson worked closely with him to perfect the movements.Reacting to the portrayal in the Michael Jackson biopic, Paterson said the film created a misleading impression that Jackson independently masterminded the entire project, including its dance sequences."Michael Peters, not Michael Jackson, created the choreography for Thriller based on his ideas," Paterson told The Sun.He further alleged that Peters had been "wiped from history" in the film and expressed concern that younger audiences watching the biopic might never learn about the choreographer's contribution."The film wiped Michael Peters, who was a great mentor, from history and I just don't want his name to be forgotten," he said.Paterson says he was deeply upset by the biopic's portrayalPaterson revealed that watching the film prompted him to contact people associated with Thriller to ensure that Peters' contribution continued to be acknowledged.He believes the story of Jackson learning from an exceptionally talented choreographer would have offered a richer and more meaningful portrayal of the singer."The story is much more interesting than the fantasy that they wanted to create in parts of the movie," he said.Paterson also emphasised that acknowledging Peters' contribution would not diminish Jackson's achievements. Instead, it would highlight the singer's willingness to collaborate with talented people and learn from them.He explained that Jackson was initially quiet during the choreography sessions, carefully observing Peters and absorbing his instructions. The singer was particularly concerned that the dancers looked like zombies and appeared genuinely frightening.However, once he understood the movements, Jackson became extremely dedicated to perfecting them. Paterson recalled how the singer would spend hours practising in front of a mirror until every movement appeared natural.He said Jackson eventually became so comfortable with the choreography that audiences could easily assume he had invented the moves himself.Thriller was not originally intended as a Halloween releasePaterson also revealed that Thriller was never specifically conceived as a Halloween project, despite becoming one of the most recognisable Halloween traditions around the world.The idea emerged from Jackson's love for horror films and his admiration for John Landis, who had directed An American Werewolf in London. Jackson wanted to collaborate with Landis on a horror-inspired musical project.Paterson pointed out that Jackson, who was raised as a Jehovah's Witness, did not celebrate Halloween."It wasn't particularly lined up for Halloween. It was just a horror kind of movie idea," he said.He added that Jackson was thrilled by the video's extraordinary success and the way fans across the world began copying its dance moves.Vincent Paterson's long association with Michael JacksonPaterson collaborated with Jackson for around two decades and was involved in several landmark performances and projects during the singer's career. His contributions included directing Smooth Criminal, co-directing and choreographing the Bad World Tour, and working on Jackson's 1993 Super Bowl halftime show and Grammy Awards performances.Apart from Jackson, Paterson has also worked with international stars such as Madonna and Paul McCartney. His film choreography credits include Evita, The Birdcage and Dancer in the Dark.Paterson spoke about his association with Jackson and the Thriller controversy ahead of receiving the Legacy Award at the 2026 World Choreography Awards, held on November 8. The honour recognises his contributions to dance and choreography.Expressing gratitude for the recognition, he said, "I'm not someone who's received many awards in my life. It's overwhelming and I'm so appreciative. It's a beautiful thing."For Paterson, however, ensuring that Michael Peters' contribution to one of the most influential music videos in history is remembered remains equally important.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Aspyn Ovard's throuple is only part of her story. 'Mormon Wives: OC' shows the heartbreak behind her new chapter in life.
articles.summary: Aspyn Ovard invites viewers into her life on "The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives: OC," from her daughter's cancer diagnosis to her unconventional relationship.
articles.body:
When the trailer for The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives: Orange County dropped, it teased plenty of dramatic storylines. Among them was influencer Aspyn Ovard introducing her ex-husband, Parker Ferris, to the married couple she's dating, a sit-down seemingly made for reality TV. But when the show premiered Nov. 12, the relationship headlines felt like a very small window into Ovard's life.

On the first episode of Hulu's SLOMW spinoff series , Ovard shares the heartbreaking news that one of the three daughters she shares with Ferris has terminal cancer . She and Ferris are parents to Cove, 7, Lola, 5, and Elle, 2, and Ovard describes the last three years of her life as "a living hell."

Long before Mormon Wives: OC , Ovard and Ferris had built an audience sharing their lives as a couple and, later, a family on YouTube. Their 2024 split after nearly nine years of marriage became internet fodder, with fans trading theories on TikTok and Reddit about what had happened. The series offers more context, sometimes in conversations that are painful to watch.

When I spoke with Ovard ahead of the premiere, she hoped viewers would come away with a fuller understanding of what she and Ferris have been going through. One scene shows them in therapy, trying to work through the end of their marriage while facing the fear of losing their daughter. I asked what it was like to film with Ferris and let viewers see how they're figuring out their relationship after divorce.

"I think it's a very accurate depiction of what our co-parenting relationship looks like," she tells Yahoo. "When you have the context of everything going on in our lives … I hope that the world can kind of see the full picture of everything and just be supportive of us and everything that we have going on and kind of just get maybe a little bit of a better understanding of why we have the relationship that we do."

Alongside those emotional conversations, viewers see Ovard falling in love, making new friends and finding moments of happiness. Moving between those parts of her life can feel like emotional whiplash, a glimpse of what it's been like for Ovard to live them all at once.

On the show, Ovard describes how abruptly her family's life changed overnight.

"Everything happened so, just out of nowhere," she says in her confessional, through tears. "One day [my daughter] was OK, and then the next day she wasn't."

"At the hospital, you're like, 'It has to be fine,'" she continues. "You can't fathom that they're actually going to tell you that your baby has cancer, and that it's terminal. She could be gone in a month, we don't know. I've been living like that for over three years, just having no idea."

Ovard keeps some details private, including which daughter is ill and the type of cancer she has. She does explain what it has meant to live between medical appointments, grateful for good news while knowing it cannot take away the larger uncertainty.

"For the past few years, we've been living scan to scan with MRIs for my daughter," she says. "We did get another stable scan this week, so I'm very grateful for that, but at the end of the day, it's very unusual for a child with this type of cancer to have this much time."

Her conversations with Ferris show how differently they are responding to that fear, even as they share it.

"Now you grab onto anything that you can to distract yourself from the grief of the fact that our daughter is going to die," she tells him during an emotional therapy session.

Ovard also explains that their marriage was struggling before the diagnosis. She says she decided to end it after learning Ferris had been drinking behind her back. When they wed, she believed they were on the same page about alcohol, a subject that carries particular weight for Ovard, whose father died from alcoholism.

"My marriage was nowhere near in a place to be able to make it through something like this," she says on the show. "We weren't even going to make it through before this happened."

Even after their split, she describes feeling responsible for taking care of him. In therapy, she tells him her work — like filming this show — has become a way to prepare financially for a future neither parent wants to imagine.

"I'm trying to make as much money as possible so that we can not have to do anything when we are grieving. So that both you and I don't have to work. You know that I will always take care of you because I always have," she tells Ferris during the therapy session.

"When everything goes to shit and things get really hard, I don't want you to have to do anything," she continues. "If you want your parents flown out here, if you want to go home, if you want to move, if you need anything, you know I will take care of it for you, because I always have."

Against that backdrop, Ovard's new relationship with married couple Briana and Billy Davies takes on a different significance. She describes how hard it has been to let people into her life and how much it hurt when some friends wouldn't get to know her partners.

"I have lost friends because of my relationship. It hurts worse than my divorce," she says on the show.

"When your child is sick, the world just goes black. You don't think that it's even possible to feel anything happy ever again," she explains. "I thought my friends would just be so happy to see me be happy, and they just didn't really have any interest in getting to know Bri or Billy, so I do hope that I find that with this group."

Her relationship with the Davises began with something she expected to be casual. Ovard initially connected with Briana, who was in an open marriage, before developing a relationship with Billy too. Ovard had sworn off dating men following her divorce. Meeting Billy changed her mind.

The new relationship also becomes part of her evolving dynamic with Ferris. In one episode, he meets the Davises and questions whether they're interested in Ovard or the followers and fame that come with her. It's one of the exchanges viewers will have in mind when she tells Yahoo they'll see him "come around a little bit."

Among her new castmates, she finds support. Bobbi Althoff, who knew Ovard before filming, says the women hadn't come in with preconceived ideas about her.

"I knew her, so I knew she was great," Althoff tells Yahoo. "And they, as soon as they met her, they also knew she was great."

For Ovard, sharing her relationship means giving viewers a chance to get to know it for themselves too. When I ask what she hopes people will see beyond the headlines, she talks about the messages she and Briana already receive.

"I think just the concept of showing something that's different and nontraditional," she says. "Bri and I get so many DMs from people that are in something similar, looking for something similar or just, you know, in a different type of relationship structure."

Those messages are part of why she wanted to let the cameras in.

"I think that having that representation is just so important for people to feel seen and feel like they can connect," she says.

She's also thinking about viewers who have little familiarity with a relationship like theirs.

"And even if they want nothing to do with the throuple or any type of different relationship, just getting to see different types of people in relationships," she continues. "I think it's just so important, literally, for everyone. It's just so good to open your mind up to all different things."

articles.title: ‘Godzilla vs. Kong’ Actress Kaylee Hottle’s Final Screen Role to Be Finished by Her Sister
articles.summary: Late actress Kaylee Hottle's older sister, Jasmine, will step in to complete the late actress’ final movie, “What Doesn’t Kill Us.”
articles.body:
"Godzilla vs. Kong" actress Kaylee Hottle's older sister, Jasmine Hottle, will step in to complete the late actress' final movie, "What Doesn't Kill Us," following her death at age 18, the film's writer and producer Andy Mingo told PEOPLE.

The actress was killed in a car accident in Maryland back in July. Her father, Joshua Hottle, previously shared the news of his daughter's passing in an emotional 23-minute-long Facebook livestream conducted entirely in American Sign Language.

"Like Kaylee, Jasmine is deaf, and her involvement allows us to honor Kaylee's memory while continuing the work she was going to be part of," Mingo said.

"Kaylee's passing was an unimaginable tragedy, and her loss is felt deeply by everyone involved with the project," he added. "When we began discussing how to move forward, the possibility of Jasmine taking on her sister's role emerged as something particularly meaningful."

"What Doesn't Kill Us" is an upcoming indie feature film directed by Anna Campbell that focuses on a group of disabled individuals who channel their experiences into superhero identities.

"For us, Jasmine stepping into Kaylee's role isn't simply a casting replacement," Mingo said. "It's an opportunity to preserve something of Kaylee's legacy while telling a story that we hope will resonate with audiences far beyond the disability community."

Born in Atlanta, Hottle came from a multi-generational deaf family. She began her career appearing in commercials, including one for video relay service Convo. It was her appearance in that commercial that caught the attention of an assistant director who worked on 2017's "Kong: Skull Island" and later recommended her to the "Godzilla vs. Kong" producers.

She made her feature film debut in that 2021 blockbuster playing Jia, the adopted daughter of Rebecca Hall's Dr. Ilene Andrews who forms a bond with King Kong through sign language. Hottle reprised the role in 2024's "Godzilla X Kong: The New Empire" and earned a Saturn Award nomination for Best Performance by a Younger Actor for her work in the film.

articles.title: In 1995, ‘Dawson’s Creek’ star Kerr Smith sold his truck and moved to New York to pursue his acting dream
articles.summary: Before becoming familiar to television audiences as Jack McPhee in Dawson’s Creek, Kerr Smith made a life-changing decision that required him to leave
articles.body: Before becoming familiar to television audiences as Jack McPhee in Dawson’s Creek, Kerr Smith made a life-changing decision that required him to leave behind the comfort of his hometown and take a chance on an uncertain future. At 23, the actor decided to pursue acting seriously, selling his truck and moving to New York City with a childhood friend.Smith has now revisited that important chapter of his life in his memoir, I Don’t Wanna Wait: My Life on Dawson’s Creek, which was released on November 10, 2026. The book offers a closer look at his journey into acting, his experiences on the popular teen drama and the moments that shaped his professional life.A high school drama class introduced Kerr Smith to actingGrowing up in Pennsylvania, Smith did not initially plan to become an actor. His interest in performing developed during his sophomore year at Henderson High School in West Chester, where he enrolled in a drama elective taught by English teacher Lorraine Moran.Smith continued exploring acting while growing up, but he did not immediately make it his career. He later attended the University of Vermont, where he studied finance and accounting rather than theatre. After graduating, he returned home and spent approximately six months working in marketing before deciding that he did not want to abandon his interest in acting without giving it a serious opportunity.He sold his truck and gave himself five years to succeedAt 23, Smith decided it was time to take a risk. He spoke to his parents about his plans to sell his Ford Bronco, use the money to relocate and start a new life in New York City with his childhood friend Matt. He had also set himself a deadline of five years to see whether he could build a career in acting.The decision was not without uncertainty, and Smith understood how difficult it could be to establish himself in the competitive entertainment industry.That encouragement remained significant to Smith even after he found success. Years later, his father admitted that he had once thought his son might end up working as a bartender. Looking back, Smith recognised how much faith his parents had placed in him when he decided to leave home.His first major acting opportunity came in New YorkSmith’s decision began yielding results sooner than he had anticipated. Within nine months of moving to New York, he secured a contract role on the daytime television soap opera As the World Turns, even before signing with an agent.He remained associated with the show for approximately 18 months. The experience gave him an opportunity to understand the demands of professional television acting and work on lengthy scripts at a demanding pace. In a 2026 interview with the University of Vermont, Smith described the experience as a form of training that helped him develop as an actor.After spending approximately two and a half years in New York, he decided to move to Los Angeles in 1998 to explore opportunities in television and film.How he landed the role of Jack McPhee in Dawson’s CreekInterestingly, Dawson’s Creek was already on Smith’s mind before he reached Los Angeles. During his cross-country journey from New York, he spent time thinking about the television projects he would love to be part of. Two shows that particularly interested him were Party of Five and Dawson’s Creek.After arriving in Los Angeles, he attended a general meeting with Kathleen Letterie, who was then a casting director for Warner Bros. During their conversation, she told him that she would find a place for him on the network.That assurance eventually turned into an opportunity. Approximately seven weeks later, Smith was offered the role of Jack McPhee on Dawson’s Creek. He joined the series in its second season in 1998, playing the brother of Andie McPhee, portrayed by Meredith Monroe.Jack gradually became one of the show’s most significant characters, particularly through his storyline involving his sexuality. His character’s coming-out journey and his on-screen kiss with another male character in the third season became an important moment in the history of American primetime television.Kerr Smith revisits his Dawson’s Creek journey in his new memoirMore than two decades after the series concluded in 2003, Smith has returned to the experience through his memoir, I Don’t Wanna Wait: My Life on Dawson’s Creek. Released on November 10, 2026, the book combines his personal experiences with behind-the-scenes accounts of the television drama.The actor has also spoken about how revisiting the show’s history helped him understand his younger self and reconnect with memories from that period. The memoir includes contributions and recollections from people associated with the series, offering readers a broader perspective on its making.For Smith, the journey from selling his truck and moving to New York to becoming part of a widely remembered television series remains an important part of his story. articles.title: Menos é Mais, Flávio Venturini, Samuel Rosa, Telo Borges e banda Ventos Solares animam fim de semana no DF | G1
articles.standfirst: Programação também conta com Tarde na Vinícola, GDV Festival e Festa do Divino. Veja o que fazer no Distrito Federal entre sexta-feira (13) e domingo (15).
articles.summary: Programação também conta com Tarde na Vinícola, GDV Festival e Festa do Divino. Veja o que fazer no Distrito Federal entre sexta-feira (13) e domingo (15).
articles.body:
O fim de semana chegou com muitas opções de lazer no Distrito Federal. Para os fãs de pagode, o grupo Menos é Mais faz um show de gravação de DVD no Mané Garrincha neste sábado (14), com um repertório que une músicas autorais e canções inéditas.

Como parte do Festival Estilo Brasil 2026, Flávio Venturini , que integrou o movimento Clube da Esquina e o grupo 14 Bis, encontra Samuel Rosa , ex-vocalista do Skank, em uma apresentação que celebra duas vozes marcantes da música nacional, nesta sexta-feira (13), no Ulysses Centro de Convenções.

Também nesta sexta, acontece, no Clube do Choro, o show "Viva Minas", em que o pianista, cantor e compositor Telo Borges se apresenta com a banda brasiliense Ventos Solares.

A programação também conta com Tarde na Vinícola, GDV Festival, Festa do Divino e peças teatrais. Veja o que fazer no Distrito Federal entre sexta-feira (13) e domingo (15):

Menos é Mais grava DVD no Mané Garrincha

Flávio Venturini e Samuel Rosa se apresentam no Festival Estilo Brasil

Fim de tarde com vinho e música na Vinícola Brasília

Remoda: festival de moda circular na Galeria dos Estados

Telo Borges e banda Ventos Solares cantam Minas no Clube do Choro

Ballet de San Petersburgo apresenta 'A Bela Adormecida'

Filme 'Água de Beber' em comemoração aos 70 anos do Catetinho

'A Casa Mágica' no Teatro Brasília Shopping

Festa do Divino – Tradição Sertaneja 3ª Edição

Neste sábado (14), o Arena Mané Garrincha vira palco da gravação do novo DVD do grupo Menos é Mais. O repertório reúne as músicas autorais que marcaram a trajetória do Menos é Mais e canções inéditas, que antecipam os próximos passos do grupo.

📍 Local: Arena Mané Garrincha, Brasília (DF)

🎫 Ingressos: a partir de R$ 460, pelo site

Samuel Rosa encerra festival em Santa Teresa, no Espírito Santo — Foto: Divulgação

Nesta sexta-feira (13), Flávio Venturini, que integrou o movimento Clube da Esquina e o grupo 14 Bis, encontra Samuel Rosa, ex-vocalista do Skank, em uma apresentação que celebra duas vozes marcantes da música nacional, no Festival Estilo Brasil 2026, no Ulysses Centro de Convenções.

Canções como "Espanhola", "Mais Uma Vez", "Me Dê Você" e "Ciranda Seco" fazem parte desse encontro inédito.

🎫 Ingressos: a partir de R$ 75, pelo site

O pôr do sol no Cerrado, uma taça de vinho e música são os ingredientes de uma experiência especial preparada pela Vinícola Brasília para este sábado (14). Das 17h30 às 21h, o espaço recebe o evento "Fim de Tarde na Vinícola", um convite para desacelerar a rotina, apreciar os vinhos produzidos na região e aproveitar a noite em um ambiente que valoriza a cultura e os sabores do Planalto Central.

A programação foi pensada para quem deseja conhecer a vinícola por uma perspectiva diferente, em um encontro que combina vinho e música com DJ do entardecer até à noite. O ingresso custa R$ 60 por pessoa e inclui a entrada no evento, uma taça e uma dose de boas-vindas de 125 ml de vinho, com opção de escolha entre branco e rosé. Ao longo da noite, os visitantes também poderão adquirir outros rótulos e opções gastronômicas disponíveis no wine bar da casa, com valores cobrados à parte.

🎫 Ingressos: R$ 60 por pessoa, com entrada, uma taça e 125 ml de vinho branco ou rosé inclusos

Reservas e informações: WhatsApp (61) 98407-5802

Neste sábado (14) e domingo (15), Brasília recebe o GDV Festival (Game Dev Festival), evento dedicado ao desenvolvimento de jogos eletrônicos e ao fortalecimento da indústria brasileira de games. A programação acontece no SebraeLAB, no Parque Tecnológico de Brasília (BIOTIC), com entrada gratuita mediante inscrição, e inclui palestras, workshops, atividades de networking e experiências práticas voltadas à capacitação e à troca de conhecimento.

Um dos destaques é a Mostra BRING, espaço dedicado à exposição de jogos desenvolvidos por estúdios independentes, que permite ao público conhecer e experimentar produções nacionais e conversar com seus criadores. O festival também contará com a GDV Jam, maratona colaborativa de desenvolvimento de jogos, e o GDV Awards, premiação que reconhece produções brasileiras em diferentes categorias.

📍 Local: SebraeLAB – Parque Tecnológico de Brasília (BIOTIC), Brasília/DF

🎫 Entrada gratuita, mediante inscrição pelo site

O Viaduto da Galeria dos Estados, em Brasília, uma nova edição do Remoda, festival de moda circular, com mais de 80 expositores, neste sábado (14). Com entrada gratuita, o evento acontece das 11h às 17h e conta com brechós, marcas autorais, artesanato e gastronomia, além de programação musical.

A programação musical terá apresentações dos DJs Fraktal e Umiranda, além de shows de Bwayne, JoJo e JWellz, que também assume o comando das pick-ups no encerramento do evento.

📍 Local: Viaduto da Galeria dos Estados, Brasília (DF)

Telo Borges faz apresentação em Campinas (SP) — Foto: Divulgação/Almanaque Café

Foi numa esquina do bairro de Santa Tereza, em Belo Horizonte, que os irmãos Borges, Milton Nascimento e um grupo de amigos criaram, nos anos 1960, um dos sotaques mais reconhecíveis da música brasileira. Parte dessa história sobe ao palco do Clube do Choro de Brasília nesta sexta-feira (13), às 20h30, no show "Viva Minas", em que o pianista, cantor e compositor Telo Borges, irmão de Lô e Márcio Borges, se apresenta com a banda brasiliense Ventos Solares e o guitarrista Haroldinho Mattos, ex-integrante do grupo brasiliense Mel da Terra.

A apresentação tem duas partes. A Ventos Solares abre a noite com canções da MPB nascidas em Minas Gerais, como "Para Lennon e McCartney", "Cais", "Ponta de Areia", "Cruzada" e "Caçador de Mim". Em seguida, o grupo passa a acompanhar Telo Borges, e a guitarra de Haroldinho Mattos se soma aos arranjos.

📍 Local: Clube do Choro de Brasília – SDC, bloco G, Eixo Monumental, Brasília

🎫 Ingressos: a partir de R$ 50, pelo site

Ballet de San Petersburgo apresenta 'A Bela Adormecida' — Foto: Divulgação

Um dos grandes clássicos do balé mundial, "A Bela Adormecida", de Piotr Ilitch Tchaikovsky, ganha os palcos de Brasília em uma montagem do Ballet de San Petersburgo. O espetáculo conta com a participação dos solistas convidados Alexander Volchkov, do Ballet Bolshoi de Moscou, e Ivan Oskorbin, do Ballet Mariinsky.

📍 Local: Ulysses Centro de Convenções – Auditório Master, Brasília (DF)

🎫 Ingressos: a partir de R$ 90, pelo site

Neste sábado (14), o Museu do Catetinho recebe exibições especiais do filme em realidade virtual "Água de Beber", que reconta como um dos maiores clássicos da bossa nova nasceu durante a construção da capital. A ação é acontece em comemoração aos 70 anos do museu.

Com cerca de oito minutos de duração, o filme recria a passagem de Tom Jobim e Vinicius de Moraes pelo Catetinho. Os dois estavam hospedados no local a convite do presidente Juscelino Kubitschek para trabalhar em "Brasília: Sinfonia da Alvorada", obra musical concebida para celebrar a nova capital.

Durante um passeio pela área verde ao redor da residência, os artistas ficaram curiosos com o som da água de uma nascente próxima. Ao perguntarem a um vigia sobre o barulho, ouviram a resposta que daria nome à canção: "Vocês não sabem não? É água de beber, camará".

📍 Local: Museu do Catetinho – Park Way, Brasília (DF)

Neste sábado (14) e domingo (15), o Teatro Brasília Shopping recebe o espetáculo "A Casa Mágica" da companhia Neia e Nando. Na peça, uma pequena criança e seu inseparável gatinho de estimação vivem aventuras surpreendentes, conhecem animaizinhos irresistíveis e descobrem que, em um mundo mágico, cada cantinho pode guardar uma novidade e cada encontro pode se transformar em uma grande aventura.

E às 18h, o Brasília Shopping recebe uma apresentação especial da Broadway Show, companhia brasiliense que une música, teatro e dança. O espetáculo acontece na Praça Central, em meio à decoração de Natal (e a atração é gratuita e aberta ao público).

🎫 Ingressos: a partir de R$ 20, pelo site

📍 Local: Temporâneo - AABB - Brasília - DF

🎫 Ingressos: a partir de R$ 100, pelo site

Nesta sexta-feira (13) e sábado (14), acontece mais uma edição do show Festa do Divino – Tradição Sertaneja, iniciativa que valoriza a música sertaneja e caipira do Distrito Federal, promovendo artistas locais e fortalecendo as tradições populares de Planaltina. O festival integra cultura, religiosidade e identidade regional, tendo como destaque o show do cantor Daniel Beira Rio.

Na programação desta 3ª edição, também estão no palco Leandro Kato, Enzo & Rafael, Boka de Sergipe e Flávio Brasil. Os DJ’s Juninho Sem Rumo e Guilherme Matuto também animam a festa. Os shows contão com intérpretes de libras.

🗓️ Quando: sexta-feira (13) e sábado (14)

📍 Local: Casa do Idosos - St. Tradicional Q 63, Lote 12, Planaltina - DF

articles.title: Flávio Venturini volta a compor com Guarabyra após 50 anos, abre parceria com Zeca Baleiro e assina uma letra no álbum que lançará em meados de 2027 | G1
articles.body:
Flávio Venturini programa o álbum 'Paisagens sonoras vol. 2' para o primeiro semestre de 2027 — Foto: Divulgação

♬ Encerrado o ciclo de comemorações dos 50 anos de carreira, celebrados em 2025 com o show e o álbum intitulados “Minha história”, Flávio Venturini abre os trabalhos promocionais do próximo álbum do artista, “Paisagens sonoras vol. 2”.

Prevista para o primeiro semestre de 2027, a sequência do álbum de 2020 é anunciado com o single “O som do sol”, disponível desde ontem, quinta-feira, 12 de novembro, com regravação da música do compositor e músico mineiro Cláudio Faria (1969 – 2017) em parceria com Murilo Antunes lançada por Faria há 17 anos no álbum “O som do sol” (2009).

Apesar da música desse single inicial ser uma regravação e não trazer a assinatura de Venturini, o repertório do álbum “Paisagens sonoras vol. 2” é essencialmente inédito e autoral.

No álbum, o cantor, compositor e pianista mineiro – um dos nomes mais importantes do universo musical do Clube da Esquina – abre parceria com Zeca Baleiro na música “O homem que rega a flor” e retoma a parceria com Guttemberg Guarabyra – com quem compôs a canção há cerca de 50 anos “Espanhola” (1977) – na valsa “A brisa do caminho e a flor”. Ambas as músicas são inéditas em disco, mas já foram apresentadas por Venturini em “Coração a dentro” (2023 / 2024), show que precedeu a turnê “Minha história” (2025).

Letrista bissexto, tendo debutado na escrita de versos com a canção “Lareira” (2024), Venturini apresenta no álbum “Paisagens sonoras vol. 2” outra composição em que assina letra e música, “Prata e luar”.

No disco, o artista também cai em samba carnavalesco – “Meu flamboyant” (Flávio Venturini e Murilo Antunes, gravado com a cantora Simone Guimarães – e canta parceria com o compositor gaúcho Vitor Hugo Santos, “Canção de acordar”.

Outra música de “Paisagens sonoras vol. 2” é “Se tiver de ser”, parceria de Tatá Spalla com Murilo Antunes. O álbum será lançado pelo selo fonográfico de Flávio Venturini, Caramelo.

articles.title: Aos 91 anos, Claudette Soares faz o presente sorrir com o álbum 'O mundo é ruim para quem não sabe esperar' | G1
articles.standfirst: Com voz suave, cantora apresenta bom repertório inédito em disco à altura da importância da artista.
articles.summary: Com voz suave, cantora apresenta bom repertório inédito em disco à altura da importância da artista.
articles.body:
Claudette Soares lança álbum com músicas inéditas à altura do passado da cantora carioca de 91 anos — Foto: Fábio Audi / Divulgação

Título: “O mundo é ruim para quem não sabe esperar”

♬ “Faço o presente sorrir / É assim que eu sei andar / [...] / A lágrima que chega / A lágrima que vai – será? – secar ”, filosofa Claudette Soares, do alto dos 91 anos festejados em 31 de outubro, através dos versos finais de “Cheguei no ponto”, música de Ana Costa e Zélia Duncan que abre o álbum “O mundo é ruim para quem não saber esperar”, lançado pela artista hoje, sexta-feira, 13 de novembro, em edição da Samba Rock Discos.

Cantora carioca celebrizada nos anos 1960 como uma das donas da bossa, após ter sido coroada Princesinha do baião na década anterior, Claudette Soares tem motivos para sorrir no presente. Idealizado por Marcus Preto e gravado com produção musical de Thiago Rabello, “O mundo é ruim para quem não saber esperar” é álbum à altura do passado honroso da artista.

Aliás e a propósito, um clima deliciosamente vintage ambienta a gravação das músicas inéditas, todas compostas para Claudette, cantora que pela primeira vez apresenta um álbum sem regravações, somente com músicas novas, ao longo de discografia iniciada em 1954, há 72 anos.

Se “Cheguei no ponto” transporta o ouvinte para um salão dos anos 1940 em que uma orquestra toca foxes e sambas-canção em clima jazzy , “Natural” abre a cortina do passado da bossa nova com os timbres do piano de Debora Gurgel e com a letra em que Nando Reis descreve paisagem à beira-mar com céu azul, em fina sintonia com a melodia aliciante do parceiro Zé Renato, nome dissociado da bossa. Tanto que, se a melodia viesse assinada por Marcos Valle, o ouvinte acharia... natural.

E por falar nesse dono da bossa, Marcos Valle brilha no álbum como o compositor de “Viva”, samba com letra de Arnaldo Antunes em que Claudette se equilibra no balanço mais agitado da bossa em feat esperto com Thalma de Freitas.

Valle contribui duplamente com o repertório, também tendo fornecido “Batuque bom”, samba composto pelo artista carioca com Tim Bernardes e gravado por Claudette com Maria Gadú (correta, mas sem a vivacidade do canto de Claudette).

Além de dividir com a anfitriã o canto de “Viva”, Thalma de Freitas é a compositora de “O que aconteceu”, samba-canção de tempo mais fechado, corroído pela mágoa e pela solidão amargadas nos escurinhos das boates.

“O que aconteceu” é a faixa que remói a sofrência pré-Bossa Nova com a elegância da sonoridade do álbum, gravado com os músicos Conrado Goys (guitarra e violão), Fábio Sá (baixo), Filipe Coimbra (guitarra) e Thiago Rabello (bateria), além da já mencionada Debora Gurgel ao piano.

“Esquecível” também revolve a memória de amor desfeito, mas com a bossa de João Donato (1934 – 2023), criador da (razoável) melodia inédita letrada pela parceira Joyce Moreno, outra dona da bossa. A banda consegue evocar no arranjo a pegada light de Donato nesse samba-canção valorizado pela interpretação de Claudette, cantora de voz igualmente suave.

“Esse escurinho e você” – parceria de Roberto Menescal (lenda viva da primeira geração da bossa nova) com Joaquim, com quem Claudette faz harmonioso feat na faixa – procura emular o balanço da bossa de Menescal, com versos que buscam a intimidade romântica da noite, sem nostalgia da modernidade vivida à luz do dia, à beira-mar.

Estranho no ninho da bossa, Leoni surpreende com “A vida é bem maior”, classuda canção evocativa de um tempo ainda sem bossa em que o compositor carioca – reconhecido nos anos 1980 pelo bom domínio do idioma pop na década em que o rock brasileiro abriu portas no mercado – nem era nascido. Acertadamente, Claudette canta “A vida é bem maior” somente com o toque do piano de Debora Gurgel.

Anunciado oficialmente em 8 de outubro com o single que apresentou “Bem feliz”, parceria de Zé Manoel com Ronaldo Bastos, o álbum “O mundo é ruim para quem não saber esperar” encerra com a primorosa balada romântica “O prazer de viver para mim é você” (2024), composta por Guilherme Arantes e gravada pelo autor com Claudette Soares em single lançado há dois anos quando o disco ainda estava em processo de gravação.

Ali, nessa grande canção atemporal de Arantes, estava o prenúncio da elegância e da sofisticação que regem o belo álbum que faz Claudette Soares sorrir no presente, com a certeza de que apresenta disco à altura da importância que tem na música brasileira.

articles.title: Em 'Carnaval de Luz', U2 não reinventa a roda, mas volta a soar como U2 | G1
articles.standfirst: Primeiro álbum de inéditas do grupo em quase dez anos tem influência latina discreta e faixas que remetem a grandes sucessos da banda.
articles.summary: Primeiro álbum de inéditas do grupo em quase dez anos tem influência latina discreta e faixas que remetem a grandes sucessos da banda.
articles.body:
Após quase dez anos sem um álbum inteiro de inéditas (o último foi "Songs of Experience", em 2017), o U2 volta com o disco "Carnaval de Luz". Assim mesmo, em bom português.

A banda passou o ano testando o território. No primeiro semestre de 2026, o U2 lançou dois EPs, "Days of Ash" e "Easter Lily". Os dois têm pontos fortes e fracos, mas mostraram que o grupo ainda tinha fôlego para novidades. Simultaneamente, a banda trabalhava em "Carnaval de Luz", disco lançado nesta sexta-feira (13).

Segundo a banda, o álbum foi inspirado pela festa no Brasil (sim, eles já vieram para a festa e, à época, Bono cantou com Ivete Sangalo e Gilberto Gil) e pelo Carnaval de outros países latino-americanos, como Trinidad e Tobago.

U2 para o disco 'Carnaval de Luz', lançado em 13 de novembro de 2026 — Foto: Divulgação

Calma: não é como se esse fosse um álbum de axé. "Carnaval de Luz" até tem discretas alusões à música latina, além de versos em português e espanhol; mas, na maior parte do tempo, é um retorno do U2 aos seus "greatest hits".

O disco abre com a enérgica "Go", firmando esse tom de rock de estádio, com uma batida marcada, mais americana do que carnavalesca. "Silencio" revisita de pegada punk, aquele de "Elevation" e "Vertigo".

Já "Greatest Show on Earth", por exemplo, é mais contemplativa e parece saída de "The Joshua Tree". E é uma das melhores músicas do U2 em décadas.

Ao longo do disco, a voz de Bono segue cristalina; o disco tem os riffs de guitarra do The Edge e todos os elementos familiares do U2 – uma banda que mantém a mesma formação desde o primeiro dia, um feito bastante raro.

Por outro lado, "Carnaval de Luz" não acerta sempre. Há algumas escolhas estranhas, como "Mirror Maker (Rosalía)", uma homenagem à cantora catalã. Essa tem um violão e estalos que até lembram, de leve, a levada flamenca. Mas bem de leve. "La Reina", em que Bono canta sobre uma "rainha do reggaeton", também é desconexa do restante.

Em alguns casos, a banda não tem as composições mais inspiradas. Isso é perceptível em “Superficiality”, cujos versos parecem mais texto de plaquinha de decoração: "You and me are breaking news / Because the news can't break us". Não ajuda que, lá pelas tantas, Bono se limite a soletrar a palavra-título.

U2 em foto do disco 'Carnaval de Luz', lançado em 13 de novembro de 2026 — Foto: Divulgação

Ao longo desse Carnaval que passa por religião, amor e reggaeton, o álbum se encerra em "Torn", dueto de Bono com Dolly Parton. A música melancólica é a última gravação em vida da cantora, morta em agosto.

"Torn" é quando o disco chega mais perto de ser político, mas ainda fica na superfície. Parece que o U2 não resiste à tentativa de fazer um hino politizado e emotivo – é a banda de "One", afinal de contas. Mas enquanto o grupo abordou bem os temas políticos dos EPs do primeiro semestre, "Torn" não tem a mesma força.

Afinal de contas, “Carnaval de Luz” não está aqui para arriscar demais. Neste disco, o U2 prefere abraçar o próprio legado, fazendo um arroz com feijão bem-vindo para os fãs.

A banda vinha de discos bem qualquer coisa e, considerando os lançamentos de 2026, dá pra dizer que o U2 se reencontrou. E tem em mãos um novo repertório que vai funcionar nos estádios, inclusive aqui no Brasil, em 2027.

articles.title: Sabotage é revivido em EP ao vivo que recupera a participação do artista em show do grupo de rap DMN em 2002 | G1
articles.body:
O rapper Sabotage (1973 – 2003) tem legado expandido com o primeiro registro ao vivo de show com áudio de boa qualidade técnica — Foto: Arte de Gustavo Amaral

♬ Em 2002, quando participou de show do grupo de rap DMN na Toco Dance House, casa da Zona Leste da cidade de São Paulo (SP), Mauro Mateus dos Santos (3 de abril de 1973 – 24 de janeiro de 2003) – o rapper paulistano imortalizado com o nome artístico de Sabotage – ainda não se tinha se tornado uma lenda do hip hop, mas já tinha lançado no ano anterior um álbum cultuado nos guetos e nas quebradas, “Rap é compromisso” (2001), e vinha ganhando visibilidade nacional, a ponto de ter participado do programa “Altas horas”, da TV Globo, naquele ano de 2002.

Decorridos 24 anos, o registro daquela apresentação de Sabotage na Toco Dance House – feita meses antes de o rapper ser assassinado, aos 29 anos – tem status de documento e é como tal que vai ser perpetuado em EP programado para ser lançado em 20 de novembro, Dia da Consciência Negra.

Com capa assinada pelo artista plástico Gustavo Amaral, o EP “Sabotage – Ao vivo – São Paulo” totaliza sete faixas, sendo que a sétima faixa, “Cigarro mata”, é apresentada como bônus por trazer música captada em show de Sabotage na cidade do Rio de Janeiro (RJ) e recuperada pelo produtor Abee. Essa música “Cigarro mata” era recorrente nos roteiros dos shows do rapper, mas permanecia indisponível nos aplicativos de áudio.

Já a gravação da participação do rapper na Toco Dance House somente existe porque o áudio do show foi captado por Diogo Poças e Eduardo Hamerschlak, que pilotavam a mesa de som da casa naquela noite de 2002.

Conservada em fita, a gravação foi restaurada e editada por Daniel Ganjaman, Fernando Sanches e Tejo Damasceno, produtores e engenheiros de som envolvidos com a preservação do legado de Sabotage.

Eternizado no EP “Sabotage – Ao vivo – São Paulo”, o set do rapper no show do DMN abarca “Abertura”, “Interlúdio” e três músicas do álbum “Rap é compromisso”. Além da música-título “Rap é compromisso”, Sabotage cantou “País da fome” (composição dividida em duas partes) e “Um bom lugar”, esta em dueto com Negro Útil.

O EP “Sabotage – Ao vivo – São Paulo” é anunciado como o primeiro registro de show do artista com áudio de boa qualidade técnica.

articles.summary: A agenda cultural Macapá destaca o 1º festival de videomapping no Mercado Central, o desfile Afro Fashion e a chegada do Papai Noel com diversas atrações gratuitas.
articles.body:
Desfile de moda afro, peça teatral e 1º festival de videomapping são atrações no fim de semana no AP — Foto: Reprodução

A agenda cultural deste fim de semana em Macapá reúne opções gratuitas e pagas de lazer entre sexta-feira (13) e domingo (15). Entre os destaques selecionados pelo g1 recomenda estão o desfile Afro Fashion Amapá, o espetáculo "Rocky Horror Beco Show" e o PerfídiaMAPPING, o 1º festival de videomapping do Estado, que transforma a fachada do Mercado Central no domingo, a partir das 19h.

O festival Quebramar 2026 encerra suas atividades no Amapá nesta sexta-feira (13) com a união do Festival Maré Vazante e da 4ª edição da periFEIRINHA. O evento ocorre na sede da Central Única das Favelas (Cufa), no Centro de Macapá, e reúne exposições de artes visuais, fotografia e mostra de curtas-metragens.

Entre os destaques está a exposição de pinturas do artista visual Wilson Toloza, inspirada nas paisagens e no cotidiano das populações ribeirinhas. Já a feira criativa reúne mais de 30 expositores de gastronomia, moda autoral, brechós, artesanato e tatuagem.

Evento conta com a 4ª edição da periFEIRINHA — Foto: Mary Paes/Divulgação

O grupo Beco Teatral apresenta o espetáculo "Rocky Horror Beco Show" nesta sexta-feira (13) e no sábado (14), às 20h, no Teatro do Sesi, em Macapá. Inspirada em um clássico da cultura pop, a comédia musical aborda a liberdade individual com humor ácido.

Na trama, o casal Brad e Janet sofre um imprevisto na estrada e busca ajuda em uma mansão misteriosa. No local, eles encontram uma convenção comandada pelo excêntrico cientista Dr. Frank-N-Furter, que está prestes a apresentar sua maior criação: Rocky.

📅 Quando: sexta-feira (13) e sábado (14)

📍 Onde: Teatro do Sesi (Avenida Desidério Antônio Coelho, s/n, bairro Trem)

Peça "Rocky Horror Beco Show" — Foto: Elielson Júnior e Lorrana Britto/Divulgação

Estilistas locais reúnem ancestralidade e moda autoral no desfile Afro Fashion Amapá, que ocorre neste sábado (14), às 19h, na sede do Sebrae, em Macapá. Com o tema "Kemet: herdeiros de um trono ancestral" , o evento destaca referências da cultura negra nas criações amapaenses.

📍 Onde: Sebrae Amapá (Avenida Ernestino Borges, nº 740, bairro do Laguinho)

Afro Fashion Amapá — Foto: Sebrae/Divulgação

As bibliotecas das unidades do Sesc Amapá estarão abertas ao público neste sábado (14) e no domingo (15) dentro da programação do "Modo Leitura". A iniciativa convida moradores a aproveitar o espaço para leitura gratuita durante o fim de semana.

A programação natalina começa neste sábado (14) no Amapá Garden Shopping, na Zona Sul de Macapá, com a chegada do Papai Noel. A recepção começa às 17h e conta com brincadeiras infantis e show gratuito da banda Chocolate com Pipoca.

📍 Onde: Amapá Garden Shopping (Rodovia Juscelino Kubitschek, bairro do Universidade)

O Mercado Central de Macapá recebe neste domingo (15), a partir das 19h, o PerfídiaMAPPING — primeiro festival de videomapping do Estado. A programação mistura arte, tecnologia e cultura regional com projeções visuais na fachada do prédio histórico.

O videomapping, também chamado de projeção mapeada, é uma técnica audiovisual que projeta imagens e animações em superfícies tridimensionais e irregulares, como fachadas e monumentos.

📍 Onde: Mercado Central de Macapá (Centro)

articles.title: 'Duran Duran' drummer Roger Taylor drops out of veteran band over tinnitus issue: ‘I’m going out on a real high'
articles.summary: Roger Taylor, beloved drummer of Duran Duran, announces his retirement due to worsening tinnitus after over 47 years with the band. He prioritizes his health while reflecting on a high point in his career.
articles.body: Duran Duran, one of the most beloved and iconic bands in the music industry, is now going to be performing with one less member. Drummer Roger Taylor has announced that he is officially retiring from the band due to a worsening health condition. The musician announced that his tinnitus has been getting worse lately, which is why he will no longer be able to perform with the band. Taylor had been with the band for over 47 years.Roger Taylor steps away from Duran Duran over worsening tinnitusA statement was shared on the band’s official Instagram page confirming the news and sharing the musician’s official statement as well. The post started off by sharing, “Roger has been at the heart of Duran Duran’s sound across two remarkable chapters. He played on the band’s era-defining early records, then returned for the celebrated reunion of the original line-up in 2001, writing and playing on six additional chart-topping albums and performing with them to millions of fans around the world. After careful consideration and medical advice, he has decided that protecting his hearing and long-term health must now come first.”Taylor also talked about how the decision was taken after careful consideration and one of the “hardest decisions” he has had to make. The drummer further added, “Playing drums in this band has been the joy of my life, and I’ll never be able to properly thank the fans for the love they’ve shown us over the years. But the truth is that my tinnitus has been getting steadily worse, and I’ve reached the point where I must now listen to my body and my doctors.” The musician also added, “Figuring out the timing of all of this has not been easy, but I’m going out on a real high," further explaining that he is ending his journey with the group on a high note, having just returned from a successful tour and being inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame.Fellow Duran Duran members also shared their statementIn the post, his fellow band members Simon Le Bon, Nick Rhodes, and John Taylor also shared their joint statement about the news of Roger’s retirement. They wrote, “Roger is our brother. His drumming helped define the sound of Duran Duran from the very beginning, and having him back with us since 2001 has been incredibly important to us all. We completely support his decision and wish him health and happiness. He will always be part of this family, while we continue exploring new and exciting projects with the band.”What is tinnitus?According to Cleveland Clinic, tinnitus is “noise in your ears, like ringing, buzzing, or clicking, that doesn’t come from an outside source." It’s often a symptom of hearing loss. But it can also be a symptom of several medical conditions. Treating the underlying condition may ease tinnitus. And there are ways to manage tinnitus that hearing loss causes. Tinnitus may go away within days or be a permanent issue.”Roger Taylor was part of the group from its inception in 1979 to 1986 and later from 2001 to 2026.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Rosalía wins album of the year for ‘Lux’ at an electrifying Latin Grammy Awards
articles.summary: Spanish singer Rosalía won album of the year at the 27th annual Latin Grammy Awards on Thursday night, capping an electrifying night full of stellar performances across genres.
articles.body: Spanish singer Rosalía won album of the year at the 27th annual Latin Grammy Awards on Thursday night, capping an electrifying night full of stellar performances across genres. Through tears, she started her speech in Spanish. “This is the third time I’ve won this award, and — just as ‘El Mal Querer’ felt like a dream, or ‘Motomami’ was a gamble — ‘Lux’ has been, for me, a leap into the void,” she said, referencing her 2018, 2022 and 2025 albums, respectively. “I believe it’s very important to speak your own truth and for others to be able to speak theirs; this album is my truth.” In many ways, it was the Spanish singer’s night from the very beginning. She opened the show live from Las Vegas’ MGM Grand Garden Arena, hosted by actor, producer and musician Roselyn Sánchez. Rosalía launched into an emotive medley of her “Lux” tracks “La Rumba Del Perdón,” “La Perla” and “Dios Es Un Stalker,” joined by angelic dancers ornamented with halos atop a stage meant to look like heavenly clouds. It was a reminder of the expansiveness of her album: an offbeat, full-hearted embrace of her classical training through huge orchestral movements, inspired by the lives of female saints. Some critics have argued that Rosalía, a white Catalan woman, should not be eligible for Latin Grammys, as she is from Spain and therefore not Latina. That clearly wasn’t top of mind with voters: Her “La Perla” also won song of the year. During her speech for that award, she thanked Mexico and invited her collaborators on the song, the American urban sierreño trio Yahritza Y Su Esencia, to join her on stage. A huge celebration for Daddy Yankee, too They call him the “King of Reggaeton” for a reason. Daddy Yankee, the 2026 Latin Grammy Awards’ person of the year and first Latin urbano artist to receive the honor, ripped through his biggest hits an hour into Thursday’s award show, treating the stage like a stadium floor. It was one for the history books: There were outfit changes, set changes and his native Puerto Rico always at the forefront as he ran through “Ella Me Levantó,” “Con Calma,” “BOTZ,” “Despacito,” “Lo Que Pasó, Pasó,” “Sonríele,” “Rompe,” “Pokito” and, of course, “Gasolina” — joined by Bizarrap, Bad Gyal, Feid, Jay Wheeler, French Montana, LL Cool J and Diljit Dosanjh. When it came time for Daddy Yankee to receive his honor, it was delivered to him by Janet Jackson “with admiration and respect,” as she said in her speech. When he accepted the award, he concluded by saying “Puerto Rico, recuerda. ... Puerto Rico no es pequeño. Pequeño el mapa.” In English: “Puerto Rico, remember. ... Puerto Rico is not small. The map is small.” A night of next-level performances Performances were at a high level: Karol G was joined by a full orchestra and 12 Mariachis for her música mexicana ballad “Ese Hombre es Malo.” Mon Laferte broke hearts with her soulful “Femme Fatale.” Silvana Estrada’s “Dime” bridged culture and heritage with her signature Venezuelan cuatro, a four-stringed instrument similar in structure to a ukulele. Brazilian superstar Anitta did a medley of her “Equilibrium” hits — “Desgraça,” “Choka Choka” and “Meia Noite” among them — an eclectic mix of Brazilian funk, samba, bossa nova, semba, reggae, electronic pop performed in Portuguese, Spanish and English. Soon after, she was back on stage accepting the trophy for Portuguese language contemporary pop album. She used her speech to shine a light on the Black culture of her native Brazil. There was a touching tribute to the late ranchera icon, Mexican singer-songwriter José Alfredo Jiménez, produced by Edgar Barrera: The Warning covered “Te Solté la Rienda,” Reik did “La Media Vuelta,” Sofía Reyes and Yami Safdie dueted “Si Nos Dejan” and Camila Fernández brought it home with a big belting “El Rey.” Not soon afterward, she headed back to the stage to perform a full-throated “Serpiente De Cascabel.” Barrera made history Thursday night: His career Latin Grammy wins now total 30 after Thursday night, making him the most awarded person in the show’s history. He surpassed records set by René Pérez with 29. That’s not all: On Thursday night, there was also a tribute to Willie Colón, the social activist and Grammy-nominated architect of urban salsa music, who died in February of this year. His son, Miguel Colón, as well as Nathy Peluso and Luis Figueroa and others performed. Feid also delighted, as did Kany García, who stunned with her acoustic, aflamencado single “La Niña Que Fui.” The Uruguayan-born Jorge Drexler’s rendition of “Las Palabras” felt like theater. And Argentine rapper Milo J performed “Solifican12” and “Gil,” joined by the Latin American folk icon Gustavo Santaolalla. Regional Mexican music stars Grupo Frontera launched into “Bye” and “Ojitos Bellos.” Carín León brought the house down with “Desde Que Te Tengo,” as did Juanes and Vivir Quintana with “Humano.” Elena Rose was joined by sword-wielding dancers for “Alma.” Venezuelan band Rawayana brought the party with “Bendito” and “Inglés En Miami.” A celebration of winners across genres The first award of the night was given out shortly after Rosalía’s opening set: Pablo Alboran and Backstreet Boys’ Howie D presented Juanes with best pop/rock album for “Juanesteban.” Trophies were handed out quickly from there. Milo J’s “Niño” was named record of the year. Karol G took home the trophy for urban music album for “Tropicoqueta.” Xavi won contemporary Mexican album for “Dosis,” his first Latin Grammy. His performance of “Dosis” and “No Capeã” closed the night. Fonseca was presented the trophy for contemporary tropical album shortly thereafter for his album, “Antes Que El Tiempo Se Vaya.” Best new artist went to Colombian singer Aria Vega, who gave her acceptance speech through tears. This year, the Latin Recording Academy made changes to the category so that only artists with fewer than three albums or 25 singles released were eligible to win. Most of the evening’s awards were handed out during a pre-televised Premiere Ceremony. That included Bobby Pulido winning the Latin Grammy for best Tejano album for his release “Bobby Pulido & Friends: Una Tuya y Una Mía (Vol. 2/En Vivo).” Just days earlier, Pulido made history in the U.S. midterm elections by securing a seat in the House of Representatives for the Democrats by flipping a Texas district seat. “I want to tell you that I’m retiring from music, and I’m leaving with so much gratitude,” he said in his acceptance speech.

articles.title: Russell Brand Accused Of Sexual Misconduct By Six More Women After Rape Conviction
articles.summary: Russell Brand has been accused of sexual misconduct and predatory behavior by six new women after being jailed for rape and sexual assault. The Times of Lond...
articles.body:
Russell Brand has been accused of sexual misconduct and predatory behavior by six new women after being jailed for rape and sexual assault.

The Times of London reported on the fresh allegations after first exposing Brand's behavior in a 2023 investigation that inspired women to report their experiences to the police. The Times ' reporting was influential in Brand being convicted last week of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault.

One woman has now alleged to The Times that Brand had sex with her without consent and then apologized afterwards. Another woman said Brand continued having sex with her, despite her telling the Despicable Me star that the intercourse was hurting. A third woman accused Brand of attempting to pull her into a lavatory in 2015, when the star was in a relationship with his wife, Laura Brand.

Brand, 51, has consistently denied wrongdoing and pleaded not guilty during his trial. He claimed that his behavior around women was "awful but lawful." During his trial, Brand said: "Consent is fundamental, essential, necessary, and in many ways more important than the sex itself." His lawyers did not respond to The Times ' request for comment on the fresh allegations.

One woman, identified as Alex by The Times , said Brand had sex with her without her consent when she was in her thirties. Alex was in a sexual relationship with Brand at the time, but alleged that the comedian had sex with her without a condom, despite her saying "no."

"He was very close, on top of me, and sort of pushing — but I knew he didn't have a condom on and I said, 'No, stop', and I started to sort of try and move. And … that wasn't happening," she said. Alex alleged that Brand apologized to her in person and by text message. "I justified it in my head by saying to myself: at least he admitted it," she added.

A second woman said Brand hurt her during intercourse after meeting the star in 2007 at a comedy gig. She was 19 at the time. "My body wasn't ready for this and it was painful", she said. "An uneasy wave hits me and I'm scared. And I say, 'It's painful' and he doesn't stop. And then it gets worse and it's really painful. And I say 'stop' and he doesn't stop." She added: "It was just like he … just wasn't present."

Another woman, who worked at a London venue Brand visited in 2015, said a member of his staff told her that "Russell wants you" and said: "He's in the disabled toilets". She alleged that Brand attempted to grab her when he claimed to need toilet paper.

In sentencing remarks following Brand's four-week trial, Mr Justice Bennathan described Brand as a "sexual predator." He said his fame protected him until 2023, when Channel 4 and The Times of London published allegations about his conduct.

The judge paid tribute to the "determination and bravery" of the women who made complaints about Brand. "Whatever women wear, wherever they go, indeed whatever they drink, they retain the right to say 'no' and to demand justice from the criminal courts when sexual predators like you, Russell Brand, act without their consent," Bennathan said.

The Metropolitan Police said several people had made fresh criminal allegations about Brand during the trial. Officers are assessing the complaints.

articles.title: 'Ramayana' box office collection day 9 (LIVE): Ranbir Kapoor, Yash, Sai Pallavi's film inches towards Rs 600 crore, enters the elite club of movies like 'Pushpa 2', 'Dhurandhar 2' which have crossed Rs 500 crore in first week
articles.summary: 'Ramayana: Rise Of A Legend' continues its impressive box office run, having crossed the Rs 1,000 crore mark in worldwide gross collections within eight
articles.body: 'Ramayana: Rise Of A Legend' continues its impressive box office run, having crossed the Rs 1,000 crore mark in worldwide gross collections within eight days of its theatrical release. The film, which arrived in cinemas on November 5, has now entered its ninth day, Friday, November 13, with its domestic earnings continuing to rise.According to Sacnilk's latest live tracking update, the film had collected Rs 39 lakh net in India by 7:03 am on Day 9, from 621 shows. The film made Rs 564 crore by the end of its first week on Thursday, November 12 and is expected to hold its momentum even over the second weekend, specially from the Friday night shows. On Day 9, till afternoon, the film has made Rs 12.79 crore. The total collection now stands at Rs 577.39 crore net in India.Meanwhile, the domestic gross has reached Rs 686 crore. These are early estimates, and the figures are expected to change as more shows report their collections through the day. Its worldwide gross currently stands at Rs 1,033.55 crore after eight days.With this achievement, 'Ramayana: Part 1' has joined the select group of Indian films to record more than Rs 500 crore in domestic net collections in their first week. The list also includes 'Pushpa 2: The Rule', 'Dhurandhar 2: The Revenge' and 'Baahubali 2: The Conclusion'. Among these films, 'Pushpa 2' was the quickest to reach the Rs 500 crore mark, managing it in five days. 'Dhurandhar 2' took six days, while 'Ramayana' and 'Baahubali 2' achieved the milestone in seven days.The first-week figures also underline the scale of the competition. 'Pushpa 2' collected Rs 688.35 crore net in its first seven days, including paid previews, followed by 'Dhurandhar 2' with Rs 624.47 crore. 'Baahubali 2' earned Rs 539 crore during the same period, while 'Ramayana' closed its first seven days at Rs 511.10 crore net. Its collection climbed to Rs 564.60 crore by the end of Day 8.The film's strong performance during the Diwali period also reflects the holiday trend at the box office. According to Sacnilk's Diwali record book, the day after Lakshmi Puja has traditionally emerged as one of the biggest days of the festive week for Hindi films.Starring Ranbir Kapoor as Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita and Yash as Ravana, 'Ramayana: Part 1' is directed by Nitesh Tiwari and produced by Namit Malhotra. articles.title: Katy Perry and Justin Trudeau step out for a casual date night in Beverly Hills
articles.summary: Katy Perry and Justin Trudeau enjoyed a casual date night in Beverly Hills, showcasing their relationship with stylish outfits and affectionate moments. Discover how they keep their romance alive away from the public eye.
articles.body: On November 11, Katy Perry and her beau, Justin Trudeau, stepped out for a date night in Beverly Hills, and fans could not get enough of the beloved couple. The two have kept their relationship away from the public eye for the most part; however, they did make their relationship Instagram official earlier this year.Katy Perry and Justin Trudeau serve couple goalsDeux Moi shared photos of the two in Bereverly Hills, stepping outside of a restaurant while holding hands, dressed in their casual bests. The singer opted for an off-the-shoulder, long-sleeved black top that she chose to pair with high-waisted light-wash jeans, black heeled ankle boots, and a small black purse. She also added a pop to her fit for the night by wearing a black-and-gold belt and earrings and having her hair styled in a sleek bun. Trudeau, 54, meanwhile, went for a cozier look for the date night and opted to wear a simple blue knit sweater that he chose to pair with jeans and black shoes.The pair have reportedly been together since around July last year. The two were first spotted in Montreal on a date together, which first sparked rumors of an ongoing romance. This was also the first time that Perry had been associated with anyone following her split with Orlando Bloom. The first time that Perry posted the former Canadian prime minister on her account was back in December 2025, and since then she has shared glimpses of their relationship with the world on her social media account.While talking to PEOPLE in September, Perry talked about her relationship and how great things had been going with Trudeau. She shared at the time, “He knows the words, he’s supportive, and he’s in awe; it’s super healing. He is really heart-centered, and I think that we align in that way.
